subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU mix, TPS & concurrency
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU mix, TPS & concurrency

Hi Alec —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick follow-up to lock down a few sizing inputs so we can put together a concrete Dedicated capacity proposal that matches Finovate AI's latency and cost tradeoffs. Notes and asks below.

Call recap (as we discussed)
- Use case: real-time customer support + smart summarization for compliance audit trails.
- Expected peak patterns: spiky during EMEA mornings, baseline in US afternoons.
- Preference: dedicated pool (data isolation + predictable TPS). Might need VPC later.

Key asks (please confirm / fill in the attached workbook):
1) Peak sustained TPS target (requests/sec) and short burst headroom (x for 10m)
2) Average request token counts and 95th percentile token length (input + output)
3) P95 latency SLO (ms) and whether 99p matters for your UX
4) Any hard constraints on quantization or model family (H100 vs A100 vs lower)
5) Timeline for pilot (start date) and expected ramp to steady state

Based on the call I want to confirm we're aligned on the following assumptions before we size:
- Target P95 latency ~150ms for single-turn generation (lower is better but raises cost)
- Workload token mix likely ~60% short (<256), 30% mid, 10% long (>1024) — please correct if off
- You prefer H100 for lower latency on long-context generation but are open to a hybrid mix for cost control

Attachments: capacity_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet) — please add the numeric answers into the "Workload" tab. Also attached a short cheatsheet (redwood-dedicated-sku-cheatsheet.pdf) that explains our typical GPU pairings.

If it's easier, we can run a 30m capacity workshop this week to walk through the workbook together — let me know two times that work (we're PDT).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

On Wed, Aug 11, 2027 at 9:12 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alec —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick follow-up to lock down a few sizing inputs so we can put together a concrete Dedicated capacity proposal that matches Finovate AI's latency and cost tradeoffs. Notes and asks below.

Thanks, Kimberly — this is great. I filled the top-level numbers inline here and will add the worksheet tonight.

Workload data (short answers):
- Peak sustained TPS: 250 req/s for 30-45m windows during peak (we see these clusters daily)
- Burst headroom: able to accept ~2.5x burst for 10 minutes (so ~625 req/s tolerated for short spikes)
- Average tokens per request: 400 tokens (input+output). 95th percentile tokens: ~1,450 tokens (longer multimodal summarizations)
- Token mix: 60% short (<256), 30% mid (256-1024), 10% long (>1024) — matches your guess
- Latency SLO: P95 = 150ms desired; P99 not critical right now but should be <500ms if possible
- Model family: prefer H100 for inference (we already benchmarked on H100 internally). Quantization: ok with 4-bit if you validate quality regressions
- Timeline: pilot kickoff target week of 2027-09-06, ramp to steady state by end of Q4

Two questions for you:
1) Do you have an initial recommendation for node counts / GPU split for a 250 TPS target (and separate estimate for burst mode)?
2) Can you confirm whether Redwood's KV/prefix cache will reduce long-token cost materially for our summarization use case?

I'll upload the workbook after lunch. Appreciate a preliminary sketch you can bring to the workshop.

—Alec
Alec Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering, Finovate AI
alec.moreno@finovate.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-12T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU mix, TPS & concurrency (internal)

Quick internal note based on Alec's numbers:
- Input data: 250 TPS sustained, 2.5x short burst, avg 400 tokens, p95 tokens ~1450. Latency P95 target 150ms. Prefers H100 and OK with 4-bit quantization if we validate quality.

Back-of-envelope sizing (very rough):
- For 250 TPS with avg 400 tokens and P95 150ms we likely need a minimum of ~6-8 H100 devices in steady state depending on batching & latency headroom. H100 gives better long-token throughput; A100s are cheaper per unit and good for batchy mid-length traffic.
- Suggested hybrid: primary pool of H100 (4-6) for low-latency long-context paths + 2-3 A100s to absorb mid-length and lower-priority batch work. Use autoscaling and burst allowance to handle the 2.5x spike instead of sizing steady state to peak.
- KV/prefix caching: should reduce per-request compute when many requests share recent context (summaries, repeated templates). For 60% short / 30% mid this could yield ~15-25% token-step reduction on average depending on cache hit rates — worth calling out in the workbook assumptions.

Operational suggestion: propose reserved (monthly commitment) for baseline + burst credits for short spikes. Price-favor A100 for batch-heavy flows and keep H100 for tail-latency sensitive paths.

I'll draft a simple node-count sketch to include in the workshop deck. Ben, can you confirm the typical burst-billing model and any SLA notes we should prep?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
